quiz.title: Laws of indices 1
quiz.instructions: Write each answer as a single power with the same base. Do not evaluate numerical powers. Assume all variables are non-zero. Choose one answer for each question.

questions.prompt: Simplify \(2^3\times2^4\). Write your answer as a single power.
questions.working:
When multiplying powers with the same base, keep the base and add the indices.

\(2^3\times2^4=2^{3+4}=2^7\).

questions.prompt: Simplify \(5^2\times5^3\). Write your answer as a single power.
questions.working:
Keep the base 5 and add the indices; do not multiply them.

\(5^2\times5^3=5^{2+3}=5^5\).

questions.prompt: Simplify \(a^4\times a^3\). Write your answer as a single power.
questions.working:
The base is a in both factors, so add the indices.

\(a^4\times a^3=a^{4+3}=a^7\).

questions.prompt: Simplify \(x^2\times x^6\). Write your answer as a single power.
questions.working:
Multiplication of powers with the same base means adding the indices.

\(x^2\times x^6=x^{2+6}=x^8\).

questions.prompt: Simplify \(3^8\div3^3\). Write your answer as a single power.
questions.working:
When dividing powers with the same non-zero base, subtract the denominator's index from the numerator's index.

\(3^8\div3^3=3^{8-3}=3^5\).

questions.prompt: Simplify \(7^6\div7^2\). Write your answer as a single power.
questions.working:
Keep the base 7 and subtract the indices; do not divide them.

\(7^6\div7^2=7^{6-2}=7^4\).

questions.prompt: Simplify \(a^9\div a^5\). Write your answer as a single power.
questions.working:
Since a is non-zero, division by its powers is defined. Subtract the second index from the first.

\(a^9\div a^5=a^{9-5}=a^4\).

questions.section: Power of a power — multiply the indices
questions.prompt: Simplify \((4^2)^3\). Write your answer as a single power.
questions.working:
When raising a power to another power, keep the base and multiply the indices.

\((4^2)^3=4^{2\times3}=4^6\).

questions.section: Power of a power — multiply the indices
questions.prompt: Simplify \((x^3)^4\). Write your answer as a single power.
questions.working:
This is a power raised to a power, so multiply the indices instead of adding them.

\((x^3)^4=x^{3\times4}=x^{12}\).

questions.section: Power of a power — multiply the indices
questions.prompt: Simplify \((a^5)^2\). Write your answer as a single power.
questions.working:
The brackets show a power of a power. Multiply the inner and outer indices.

\((a^5)^2=a^{5\times2}=a^{10}\).
